summary: Tested the 1h follow-up scans (Bybit + HotForex) and the per-position AI analysis buttons from end to end. Backend: 31/31 pytest pass (test_followup_and_analyze, test_manual_manage, new test_followup_api_public over the PUBLIC URL, all with the real LLM). Ran a simulated Bybit follow-up scan (scan_once(followup=(1,5))) against a scratch DB. It behaved as specified: keys end in :seg1, no shadow trades, the pair with an open position is skipped, the same follow-up index is de-duplicated, the whole follow-up is skipped with a log line at max positions, live_candle 'vela 1h en curso (minuto X/60)' plus rejection is in the context and prompt_line, and signals open when approved. Frontend, Bybit and HotForex: the first column of the positions table is 'HERRAM.'. The chart button opens position-chart-dialog, and fullscreen toggles between 1152x894 and 1920x1080 and back. The AI button opens a dialog: Cancel sends 0 requests, Opinion shows 'Solo opinión: no se ha cambiado nada', and Act shows 'Acción aplicada: se mantiene sin cambios'. Each AI call takes about 4 s. The settings fields 'Seguimientos tras el cierre (1h)' and 'Cada cuántos minutos' save and persist after reload (restored to 5/5). Pepperstone: no follow-up fields; positions render as cards with GRÁFICO but no AI button. All test positions were closed and settings were restored.

minor.issue: Ignores pending_entries (queued maker entries). With the default entry_order_type=maker, a pair or slot held by a pending maker order is not skipped up front. _handle_signal still blocks it ('orden límite en espera' / slot block), so nothing is opened twice. The only cost is extra klines fetches and a FILTER log line for every follow-up.
found += 1 runs before the signal_keys dedupe in _handle_signal. A re-run of the same follow-up index logs 'N señales sin ejecutar re-evaluadas' even though nothing was re-evaluated (cosmetic).
atr = float(df.iloc[-2]['atr'] or 0): a NaN ATR is truthy, so range_atr becomes nan and the rejection size check is skipped. Only possible with very short history.
Exists through the shared routes even though the Pepperstone UI hides it. Harmless, but it can still be called on the EMA-only bot.
Unlike the auto review path, there is no guard for exit_mode=='cross' (EMA-test) positions, so manual 'act' can move the stop of a cross trade to breakeven. Check whether this is intended.

issues: For about 1 s after opening, the chart area shows a dim, empty canvas while the chart loads. Acceptable; a skeleton or spinner could be added.

action_items: Optional: include pending_entries in followup.pairs_to_skip (symbols and slot count)
Optional: count 'found' in follow-ups only when the key is new
Optional: decide whether manual 'act' BREAKEVEN should be blocked for exit_mode=='cross' positions, as the auto path does
critical_code_review_comments: The scheduling is correct. Follow-ups run only when engine.followups and not candle_only and tf=='1h' and followup_scans>0. pending() uses a 240 s window and t>last. The next wake is min(next close, next follow-up). Slots with k*every>=60 are dropped. If asyncio wakes a few ms early, the loop re-sleeps 0.5 s and then fires.
FxEngine.followups = not ema_only, so Pepperstone is off. LabEngine has candle_only, so both Labs are off. Follow-ups return early when the forex market is closed.

Follow-up blocks are only logged (no signal doc, no shadow trade). Approved follow-ups go through the same rules/AI/late-entry path. The live candle is injected into ai_funnel (2 prompts) and ai_advisor._build_prompt.

Test isolation: test_manual_manage and test_followup_and_analyze both opened BTCUSDT on /api in parallel xdist workers. This caused an intermittent 'posición ya abierta' failure (1 in 2 runs). Fixed by switching test_followup_and_analyze to SOLUSDT/USDJPY.
